newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt advocates long-term aid to east Germany.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt advocates long-term aid to east Germany.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Thursday that formerly communist eastern Germany would need a high level of state aid to aid its economic regeneration into the 21st century.
Speaking in a debate in the Bundestag lower house of parliament on a bill to extend aid to the east after 1998, Rexrodt said maintaining current funding levels was vital.
"With this new concept, state aid will be maintained at a high level," Rexrodt said.

The Bonn coalition and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Wednesday agreed modest changes to Rexrodt's subsidy programme, paving the way for the bill's passage through both the Bundestag and the Bundesrat upper house.
According to the bill, 5.7 billion marks will be made available per year from 1999 onwards in the form of investment bonuses for companies.
"The east German economy, which is already developing better, will thus gain extra momentum," Rexrodt said.
Bundestag deputies were due to vote on the bill shortly. A final lower house vote on Finance Minister Theo Waigel's two-year package of sweeping tax cuts was also imminent.

Unlike Rexrodt's subsidy bill, Waigel's tax reforms are expected to be blocked next week by the SPD majority in the Bundesrat, sending the package into parliament's tortuous conflict resolution process.
